newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine postal sale hits snag, new bids in 72hrs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine postal sale hits snag, new bids in 72hrs.

text.p: The sale of a 30-year concession to run Argentine state post office Encotesa hit a delay Monday after it was ruled the difference between the two top bids was too narrow and new bids must be made in 72 hours.

Encotesa chief Arturo Puricelli told a confused bid-opening ceremony, where an Argentine group had already been declared winner with a $51 million fee offer, that the sale rules established that difference between the top bids had to be at least 5.0 percent.

Encotesa had announced a few moments earlier that local firms Itron and Sideco, controlled by Grupo Macri, and Banco de Galicia, with the technical support of the British state post office, won the bidding with their offer of a $51 million six-monthly fee.

But it was then ruled that the difference with the $48.5 million bid from Argentine companies TAC and ROMAN, together with local tycoon Samuel Liberman, owner of cable TV firm VCC, and Germany's state post office, was too slim.
"The difference between the two main bids was a little under five percent and the prospectus establishes that they will have to make two new bids in 72 hours," said Puric elli.

The lowest bid was $30.77 million from local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding company controlling Telefonica de Argentina, and New Zealand's Infratil International, backed by the New Zealand Post.
COINTEL is owned by Telefonica de Espana, operator of Telefonica de Argentina, and Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holding SA.

After the first erroneous announcement, Itron's President Luis Cudmani said his group would start running Encotesa on September 1 and promised customers "a gradual improvement in the quality of service."
The Encotesa privatization has already been troublesome after three groups protested their disqualification from the bidding. At least one of them, led by Brazilian airline VASP, is suing.
VASP was disqualified because according the sale commission it did not present a complete investment plan.

The two other groups disqualified, one led by Dutch ING Bank-NV Cayman Islands, the other by Argentine construction group Benito Roggio e Hijos SA, were disqualified on the grounds that they did not have the technical support of an official post office, as set down in the prospectus.
The privatization decree was signed in March and sets a minimum investment requirement of $25 million a year.
